rawSources.locator: L55: stiffened petticoats and the word crinoline first referred to a horsehair-and-linen fabric; L62-L63: cage crinoline emerged in 1856, with steel hoops increasing in diameter toward the hem and supporting wide skirts without burdensome petticoats; L77-L78: crinolette had a flat front and rear half-hoops, bridging cage crinoline and bustle; L89-L90: bustle/tournure supported skirts gathered at the back and projecting below the waist.
rawSources.title: Corsets, crinolines and bustles: fashionable Victorian underwear

literal.prompt: Как называли появившуюся в 1856 году опору из стальных обручей, расширявшихся к подолу и поддерживавших широкую юбку без множества тяжёлых подъюбников?

literalGroups.primaryGround: The V&A says a cage crinoline emerged in 1856; it was built from steel hoops increasing toward the hem and supported wide skirts without burdensome petticoats (L62-L63). It contrasts other answers: bustle/tournure projected gathered skirts at the back (L89-L90), crinolette had a flat front and rear half-hoops (L77-L78), and layered/quilted petticoats supplied earlier volume (L55). The date, cage construction, and all-around widening support the unique key.

literalGroups.literal: Клеточный кринолин появился в 1856 году: его стальные обручи расширялись к подолу и поддерживали широкие юбки без тяжёлых подъюбников. Кринолет позднее имел плоский перед и полуобручи сзади, а турнюр создавал объём за телом.
literalGroups.primaryGround: V&A directly supports the 1856 date, expanding steel hoops, and replacement of burdensome petticoats (L62-L63); its later crinolette and bustle descriptions support the stated distinctions (L77-L78,L89-L90).

literalGroups.literal: В 1870-х турнюр поддерживал юбку, собранную сзади и выступавшую из-за линии талии.
literalGroups.primaryGround: V&A calls the bustle a distinct undergarment of the 1870s and explains that it supported skirts gathered at the back, projecting below the waist; it also gives tournure as its French name (L89-L90).

literalGroups.literal: Слово «кринолин» сначала обозначало жёсткую ткань из конского волоса и льна; позднее так стали называть и саму нижнюю конструкцию.
literalGroups.primaryGround: V&A says stiffened petticoats were made from woven horsehair and linen fabric called crinoline, and that the name later came to denote the garment too (L55). This is an additional fact about the correct option.

literalGroups.literal: Кринолет имел плоский перед и полуобручи сзади; он стал переходной формой между клеточным кринолином и турнюром.
literalGroups.primaryGround: V&A describes a crinolette as a modified crinoline with flat front and rear half-hoops, bridging the cage crinoline and full bustle (L77-L78).

literalGroups.literal: Стёганые подъюбники создавали объём слоями; такая опора делала широкие юбки тяжёлыми и жаркими.
literalGroups.primaryGround: V&A says broad early Victorian skirts gained volume from numerous, including quilted, petticoats; these were heavy and hot, while the 1856 cage was a lighter alternative (L55,L62-L63).
